findings.summary: The escalation can keep the planner's effort the same or lower it: the override replaces the effort instead of raising it
findings.evidence: Step 3 sets `spec.effort = cfg.thrash_effort.as_str().to_string()` whenever `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. The first call's effort comes from `effort_for(Planner)`, which is `verifier_effort` (config.rs:830, athena.toml:21, now `high`). Nothing orders the two values. If an operator sets `verifier_effort = "max"`, the default `thrash_effort = xhigh` makes every re-plan run below the first call, the opposite of the request ('increase intelligence') and of the reading ('runs at a higher effort than the first'). The plan's own risk note ('an operator can set `high` to turn escalation off') shows it treats this as a replacement, not a raise. Fix: Derive `PartialOrd, Ord` on `EffortLevel`, in the order low < medium < high < xhigh < max. Parse the base `spec.effort` into an `EffortLevel` and set the effort to the higher of the base and `thrash_effort`. Alternatively, have `validate()` refuse a `thrash_effort` below `verifier_effort`. Add a config or run test where `verifier_effort = "max"` and the re-planned call stays at `max`.

findings.summary: The criterion 6 'fails without' claim is wrong: the repository-config assertion passes even when athena.toml lacks the key
findings.evidence: The plan asserts that the repository config has `thrash_effort == Xhigh` and says that 'without the athena.toml key the repository-config assertion that it is set explicitly fails'. The serde default is also `Xhigh`, so `Config::parse(REPO_CONFIG)` gives `Xhigh` with or without the key, and the assertion cannot fail. Fix: Either assert on the text of the `[job_plan]` table of `REPO_CONFIG` (for example, that it contains a line starting `thrash_effort`), or set a value in athena.toml that differs from the default. Otherwise, call criterion 6 an inspection and drop the claim.

findings.summary: A second list of effort names can drift from EFFORT_LEVELS
findings.evidence: `EFFORT_LEVELS` (config.rs:337) validates the `[models]` efforts. The new `EffortLevel` enum hard-codes the same five names through serde `rename_all` and `as_str()`. If someone adds a level to one and not the other, the two accept different values. Fix: Add a unit test that the `as_str()` values of `EffortLevel`'s variants equal `EFFORT_LEVELS` in order. Alternatively, have `as_str` index into `EFFORT_LEVELS`.

findings.summary: An unknown value fails in a different way from the other effort keys, which the reading said it would match
findings.evidence: The `[models]` efforts are refused in `validate()` with `ConfigError::Effort(name, value)` (config.rs:665-676). The enum is refused earlier, by serde, as `ConfigError::Parse`. The plan acknowledges this. The refusal still names the value and the key, because toml's error quotes the source line, so the `bad_job_plan_settings_are_refused_naming_the_field` row passes. Fix: Keep the enum, but state the difference in D178 and the CHANGELOG bullet. Also have the new test assert that the error names both `thrash_effort` and `extreme`.
findings.location: Risks, second bullet; Reading assumption 'Config validation refuses an unknown value, the same way as the other effort keys'

findings.summary: Text-based readers of athena.toml's [job_plan] table are left out of the dependents list
findings.evidence:
hestia.rs asserts that athena.toml contains the exact text `[job_plan]
enabled = true
mode = "hard"
` and rewrites it. `repository_job_plan_config` copies the table from `[job_plan]` up to the next `[` line. Appending the key and its comment after `max_rounds` (step 4) keeps both working. A comment or the key placed between `[job_plan]` and `mode` would break the hestia assertion. Fix: Add both readers to the dependents list. In step 4, state that the comment and key go after `max_rounds = 5` and that the first three lines of the table stay unchanged. The tests are hestia's dormant-stage tests and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test job_plan`.

findings.summary: A seeded plan from an earlier job that stopped in planning is the clearest thrash signal, but it runs at base effort
findings.evidence: `resumed_from` (planning.rs:39-52) seeds round 1 with a kept plan from a job that has already used its rounds. Criterion 2 explicitly keeps the first attempt of round 1 at the configured effort, so the plan follows the reading. Fix: No change is required. Mention in D178 that escalating across jobs was considered and deferred, so a later job can widen the trigger on purpose.

summary: The plan reads the request correctly and changes the code at the right place. In `planning_round` (planning.rs:140-155) it overrides `spec.effort` after `agent_spec`, which is the same pattern as producer.rs:339-341. Both triggers are already in `Attempt`, and the critic spec and the first call are left alone. I read the code and confirmed the seams it names: `repo_with_planning`, `planning_script`, `bad_plan`/`good_plan`, `revising_critique`/`accepting_critique`, and `Records::load` at tests.rs:1116. I also confirmed that `invoke_and_record` copies `spec.effort` into the record (invocation.rs:202), and that the only struct literal of `JobPlanConfig` is its `Default`. I grepped for other readers of `job_plan` and of invocation effort and found none the change breaks. Two text-based readers of athena.toml, hestia.rs:3579 and cli job_plan.rs:1125, still work if the key is appended at the end of the table. One soundness problem remains. The override sets the planner's effort to `thrash_effort` unconditionally, so if `verifier_effort` is set at or above it (for example `max`), the "escalation" keeps the same effort or lowers it. That contradicts the reading's "higher effort than the first". The other findings are minor.
